{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the belly line, stroke 2, which is the whole lower outline of the fish and about a third of the standing dominoes. I laid about 40 dominoes in one continuous run from the nose, and every one connected. That gave the fish its full body shape, so the outline reads as a fish. I stopped at the middle of the bottom so the tail stretch could pick up from my line's end.

Execution: I took the belly stroke early and worked steadily on it from the nose until it was finished. I stood back up the one domino that needed it. I then used inspection to check the upper tail join. I found about a dozen dominoes still unconnected and reported it, so the team could close the gap. Before the push, the whole fish was dark from the start.

Collaboration: I stated clearly which stroke was mine. I asked that the belly not be laid from both ends, to avoid a messy joint. I agreed to hand the last stretch to Priya at the midpoint, and I kept clear of the joints others were closing. When it was time, I kept my hands off so nothing got bumped.

Leadership: I took ownership of a large, critical piece without needing direction. I communicated my progress and handoff points plainly so others could plan around me. I flagged the unconnected tail section when I saw it, and I helped hold the table to a hands-off finish.", "my_share_percent": 30}
